newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil up following crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil up following crude.

text.p: Euro low sulphur straight-run fetched a largely steady price on Tuesday but some sellers increased their price on the back of higher futures, traders said. They said a refiner sold a prompt loader of low sulphur straight-run to an independent trader at $110/$112 fob Sines, compared with $110/$112 that a cargo fetched on Friday.
But one seller of 0.5-0.7 percent sulphur material said he was offering at $117/$118, compared with $115 on Monday, after crude futures gained.
"It is just following crude," the seller said.
Other trades said that Tuesday's seller could not have got a better price as the cargo was quiet prompt and only two other buyers bid lower, about $108 fob a tonne and $115 cif a tonne respectively.

Shipping sources said the independent trader was looking for 40-80,000 tonnes of high sulphur straight-run out of Ventspils and Tallin for August 15-20 loading to go to the U.K., the Mediterranean or Trans-Atlantic.
Russian high-sulphur straight-run was also offered stronger.
Traders said two E-4s were on offer at a strong three means plus $5, or $2 up on last done, but some doubted they would fetch that figure.
Two M-40s were at two means plus $4, or $1 higher than earlier in the day.
